title: Live median latency
prompt:
A monitoring service receives latency samples one by one; after each sample, report the median of all samples received so far.

- nums: 1 to 50,000 integers between -10^6 and 10^6, in arrival order.
- With an odd count the median is the middle value; with an even count it is the mean of the two middle values (which may end in .5).
- Return a list of len(nums) medians, one after each sample.
hints: Re-sorting after every sample costs O(n log n) each time. You only ever need the one or two middle values.
Split the samples into a lower half and an upper half: a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half.

Insert into the lower heap if the value is <= its top, otherwise into the upper heap; then move one top across so the lower heap has the same size as the upper or exactly one more. The median is the lower top, or the average of both tops when sizes are equal.

solution.explanation: The max-heap holds the smaller half and the min-heap the larger half, with every lower value <= every upper value. After each insert at most one element moves between heaps to restore the size balance, so the middle values are always the heap tops. Each sample costs O(log n).

complexity.notes: O(log n) per sample and O(1) to read the median. Sorting after every insert would be O(n^2 log n).

followUps: Report the median of only the last w samples (a sliding window). How do you remove samples that fall out of the window?
